hints.content: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to{-6}^-}h(x)$ represents the limit of $h$ as $x$ approaches $-6$ *from the left*.

Since we're only interested in how the function behaves as it approaches $x=-6$ from the left, we only need to look at this part of the table:

$x$ | $-6.125$ | $-6.025$ | $-6.005$ 
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: 
$h(x)$ | $3.96875$ | $3.99875$ | $3.99995$

The $h(x)$-values seem to approach $4$.

choices.clue: A limit from the left does not have to be negative.
This is the limit as $x$ approaches $-6$ from the right, not the left.
The function appears to approach a specific function value from the left.
